dialogue_quality_notes: Participants negotiated concrete conditions and repeated key points (extractor/window/wash up) until consensus — e.g., Agent B's conditions in Turn 4 were accepted in Turn 5 and reiterated in Turn 7.

Agent A twice requested not to be singled out ('please don't single me out' and later 'Don’t single me out in front of everyone'), which is a social concern rather than a substantive barrier to agreement.
C takes the coordinator role (proposing rules, offering to set the rota) which helped move toward resolution.
evaluation.final_reason: The household agreed concrete rules resolving the primary incompatibilities: immediate dishwashing by the cook, a late-cook priority slot for whoever arrives last, and required mitigations (use extractor, open window, wash up immediately, avoid strong-smelling food or notify others). Evidence: Turn 5 — Agent C: 'Everyone washes their own dishes after cooking; late-cook follows Agent B's conditions.' Turn 7 — Agent A: 'Late-cook is whoever gets home last; they must use the extractor, open the window, and wash up straight away.' Turn 8 — Agent D: 'Okay, agreed.' These lines show the core demands were specified and accepted by the parties.
position_change_notes: Agent C: initiator and mediator — proposed washing rule and took on setting the weekend rota; maintained consistent position.
Agent D: initially complained about stove use but quickly accepted the late-cook slot and conditions ('I'm fine with any weekend' and Turn 6 confirmation), shifting from complaint to agreement.

Agent A: was the subject of the complaint but accepted the washing rule and late-cook conditions while requesting not to be singled out (Turn 3 and Turn 7); softened defensive stance and agreed to terms.
Agent B: started with a complaint and then moved to offer detailed constraints for late-cook (Turn 4) and accepted the final arrangement; shifted from protest to conditional cooperation.
No participant refused or retracted agreement after Round 4; positions converged through adding and accepting specific conditions.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent C directly asks Agent A to wash the pan and proposes a household rule: 'everyone washes their own dishes right after cooking, and we have a weekend rota for deeper clean.' Turn 2 — Agent D accepts washing but adds a new demand for a nightly 'late-cook' slot. Multiple incompatible expectations about kitchen use and responsibilities are asserted but not yet reconciled.

Turn 3 — Agent A accepts the washing rule and late-cook slot but asks not to be singled out and adds conditions: 'must wash their pans straight away, use the extractor, and not leave smells.' Turn 4 — Agent B accepts the late-cook slot with detailed conditions (extractor, open window, avoid strong-smelling food, notify others). Parties are negotiating specific conditions rather than opposing each other, reducing but not eliminating substantive disagreement.

Turn 5 — Agent C accepts Agent B's conditions and offers to set a weekend rota: 'Everyone washes their own dishes after cooking; late-cook follows Agent B's conditions.' Turn 6 — Agent D confirms acceptance and repeats the nightly-slot conditions. The group converges on the same set of rules; only administrative details remain unsettled.

Turn 7 — Agent A: 'Late-cook is whoever gets home last; they must use the extractor, open the window, and wash up straight away.' Turn 8 — Agent D: 'Okay, agreed. I'll follow those conditions when I'm the late-cook.' All named parties accept the core substantive rules (washing, extractor/window use, late-cook definition), resolving the primary incompatibility about smells, stove access, and dishwashing responsibilities.

Turn 10 — Agent B signals exit ('I'll try to sleep now'). Turn 11 — Agent C begins assigning the weekend rota and asks Agent A to pick a weekend; no objections are raised. The substantive conflict (kitchen use and smells) has been settled; only routine scheduling remains.

Turn 12 — Agent D accepts the assigned weekend. Turn 13 — Agent C confirms and presses Agent A and Agent B to confirm their weekend choices later. No substantive objections are raised; the agreed rules stand.

substantive_insights: The main tension was between individual cooking needs/schedules and collective nuisance (smells and shared cleaning duties).

A procedural solution combining a behavioral rule (wash up immediately), an access rule (late-cook priority for whoever arrives last), and mitigation measures (extractor + open window + avoid strong smells or notify) addressed both access and nuisance concerns.
Cleaning responsibility and deep-clean scheduling were separated (immediate washing vs weekend rota), lowering friction by dividing tasks into daily behavior and periodic shared chores.
Remaining administrative items (final assignment of weekends for A and B) are not substantive conflicts but required follow-up.
